correctness.rationale: An absent-species indicator derivation supplies exact integer hypergeometric second moments. The attached executable exhaustively enumerates every positive-integer partition of N<=8 and every permitted one-unit transfer, with 0,0,1,2,5,9,17 candidate pairs for N=2,...,8; the only double reversal occurs at (4,3,1)->(4,2,2). Independent direct combination enumeration agrees with all seven differences. For arbitrary k>=1 the strict inequalities at sample sizes 2,3,7 are proved by displayed exact rational polynomial coefficient vectors in t=k-1>=0 (all coefficients one fixed sign). The checker expands and checks every coefficient and evaluates selected independent binomial formulas. Formula (2) proves the strictly increasing means. The finite search is not used as a proof for arbitrary k.

evidence: Gotelli and Colwell, mean rarefaction curves may cross twice for arbitrary community comparisons; formula (2) in the new proof makes mean richness monotonically larger after balancing.
Nipperess and Matsen establish moment formulas for arbitrary phylogenetic marked samples, including a star-tree case, but make no transfer-specific reversal-count claim in inspected sections.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The already known general formulas allow the new comparison to be computed, but do not by themselves state the nontrivial global sharp threshold. The prior mean-curve crossing statement applies to different pairs not ordered by the strict balancing transfer and therefore cannot cover the positive-mean yet twice-reversing variance phenomenon. A previously accessible finite census for mean-richness reversals compares arbitrary abundance partitions and has a different statistic; it neither implies nor is implied by the present variance theorem.

originality.rationale: The original mathematical contribution is the constrained-sign-reversal sharp minimum, unique eight-person witness, and all-size positive-coefficient sign certificate, not the known expected-richness or variance formulas. Literature on rarefaction means and generalized variance formulas was substantively inspected; no source found deriving the stated one-transfer variance transition. A classical 1975 source was abstract-only, so equivalent prior work remains a genuine possibility and bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Heck, van Belle and Simberloff (1975) is highly relevant and was accessible only through abstract and secondhand citation; the article cannot be classified as definitively non-covering.
A synonymous extremal theorem in finite-population occupancy, majorization, or reliability literature might be overlooked despite targeted searches.
Independent bibliographic auditing is not performed.

value.rationale: Species-abundance evenness is central to ecological diversity measurement, and expected rarefied richness increases monotonically with balancing. The new theorem proves uncertainty can still oscillate twice as sampling effort changes, isolates the smallest possible census over all integer partitions, establishes uniqueness at the first occurrence, and shows robustness of this behavior at arbitrarily large census sizes through a one-parameter abundance family. This is a mathematically motivated comparison, not a routine restatement of the hypergeometric variance formula.
